title: Pedal notes, modern high-note playing and rock and roll
summary: He says players no longer use pedal notes, and compares traditional jazz to rock and roll.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: That reminds me, is there anybody around that really gets down and plays those pedal notes like they used to? I never have understood what happened to- On the trumpet? Yeah, like trumpet players. What happened to pedal notes playing?

Very few of them. That's what I was telling you just a while ago, but if you're listening to Louis Armstrong, and you were just like hearing Buddy P.T. You make those little notes. They don't seem to do that much anymore. Everybody wants to make high notes. In the modern style everybody wants to play flute parts. Trombone, trumpets, everything. Play out all of them. Play up like a flute and make a lot of notes. Who can make the most notes? There's a lot of different, she traditional, they're not interested in making a lot of notes. They want to make the feelings to make you feel. That's why I say this late rock and roll music that they play, and it's more like traditional jazz than any other music from that time. Even from, it's more even than the Dixaland and Bop music. All that late music that came out, all that fast work. But some of those records that you hear now, with the rock and roll, it's just like that traditional jazz. You hear how the bass player hitting each note.
